title: Cybersecurity Budgets Are Growing Fast. AI Threats Are Growing Faster.
gist: A survey of ~300 cybersecurity leaders finds cyber spending grew 12% in 2025 against an expected 7%, with over 80% still raising budgets into 2027, yet AI is expanding the attack and protection surface faster than money can absorb: 89% of companies saw AI-enabled attacks in the past year while only 41% have formal AI governance and under 20% run shadow-AI monitoring or prompt-injection detection. The investable conclusion is that AI accelerates rather than cannibalizes cyber demand, but buyers are consolidating vendors in 18 of 24 product categories and paying only for demonstrable differentiation, squeezing mid-tier and me-too AI-branded players.

themes.theme: Cyber budget resilience and its ceiling

insights.claim: Enterprise cybersecurity spending grew 12% in 2025, well above the 7% that had been expected, making it one of the most resilient areas of enterprise technology spending.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 5-point upside surprise to consensus cyber spend growth argues for owning security budget beneficiaries over broader enterprise software, where budgets are less defensible.
insights.quote: Overall cyber spending grew by 12% in 2025, well above the expected 7%
insights.locator: Cyber spending continues to rise, but some categories

insights.claim: More than 80% of roughly 300 surveyed cybersecurity leaders say they will keep increasing their budgets into 2027.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Gives roughly a two-year visibility window on security demand, supporting multi-year revenue models for cyber vendors even if broader IT spend softens.
insights.quote: with over 80% of respondents continuing to increase budgets into 2027
insights.locator: AI is expanding the cybersecurity challenge faster

insights.claim: Most CISOs expect the AI-driven portion of budget increases to persist only another one to two years before spending normalizes, implying the current surge is a bulge rather than a permanent step-change in growth rate.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sets a rough 2027-2028 clock on the AI-security spending upcycle; multiples paid on the assumption of a permanent re-rating carry deceleration risk.
insights.quote: Most CISOs expect AI-driven budget increases to continue for another one to two years before spending normalizes.
insights.locator: Cyber spending continues to rise, but some categories

insights.claim: Cloud security, data security, and threat intelligence are the highest-priority product categories, with more than half of CISOs planning to increase spend in each.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Names the three sub-sectors where budget dollars are most likely to land; other cyber categories should be underwritten on share gain, not category growth.
insights.locator: The specific security product categories of cloud, data

insights.claim: Rising security budgets are being spread across a materially larger mandate, so headline budget growth overstates real capacity gains for security teams.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Vendors that genuinely reduce workload or headcount need have pricing power; incremental point tools compete for a budget that is effectively shrinking per unit of scope.
insights.quote: Budgets are increasing, but complexity is increasing faster.
insights.locator: This is the new reality for CISOs

insights.claim: Companies are expected to scale back spending in other areas to reallocate resources into the security solutions that matter most.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Cyber growth may come at the expense of adjacent IT line items, so the trade is long security versus other enterprise software rather than long IT spend broadly.
insights.locator: Bottom-line Implications

insights.claim: CISOs must now build controls for models, agents, copilots, prompts, training data, synthetic data, AI-generated code, and non-human identities on top of the traditional estate of networks, endpoints, cloud, applications, data, identities, and third parties.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Each named asset class is a potential new product category and TAM line; use the list as a screen for which AI-security startups address real, budgeted control gaps.
insights.locator: AI is expanding what organizations need to protect

insights.claim: Only 41% of surveyed organizations have formal AI governance policies and just 23% apply monitoring or logging to AI agents.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sub-25% penetration in agent observability is the clearest greenfield in the survey; early leaders in that category face a mostly unpenetrated installed base.
insights.quote: Only 41% of respondents have formal AI governance policies in place, and only 23% have applied monitoring or logging to agents.
insights.locator: Most companies have adopted minimal AI-specific security controls

insights.claim: Fewer than 20% of organizations have adopted shadow AI monitoring, prompt injection detection, or non-human identity governance.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Three named categories with under 20% adoption and demonstrated efficacy are the highest-slope adoption curves to underwrite in AI-security venture and growth deals.
insights.locator: Most companies have adopted minimal AI-specific security controls

insights.claim: CISOs with higher adoption of AI-specific controls were far less likely to report significant impact from exploited AI vulnerabilities, data leaked to AI tools, or employee shadow AI use.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Measurable outcome correlation is the ROI argument that converts these low-penetration categories from experiments into budgeted line items; watch for it in vendor case studies.
insights.quote: CISOs that have higher adoption of these controls were far less likely to report significant impact from AI vulnerabilities being exploited, data leaked to AI tools, or shadow AI use among employees.
insights.locator: Yet our data shows that these measures are well-correlated

themes.theme: Attack economics inverted by frontier models

insights.claim: The long-anticipated scenario of AI agents cracking complex cyber defenses stopped being hypothetical with the recent release of several frontier AI models that can identify and exploit software vulnerabilities at previously unimaginable speed, scale, and autonomy.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Marks a discrete regime change in offense cost curves that resets the required run-rate of defensive spend rather than merely extending a trend.
insights.quote: AI is changing the economics of attack
insights.locator: At the same time, AI is changing the economics of attack

insights.claim: One frontier model identified thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities across major operating systems and browsers, including flaws that had survived years of human review and automated testing.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Existing code bases carry far more undiscovered exploitable surface than assumed, which favors patch-velocity, runtime protection, and threat-intelligence vendors over static assurance approaches.
insights.quote: One identified thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities across major operating systems and browsers, including flaws that had survived years of human review and automated testing.
insights.locator: At the same time, AI is changing the economics of attack

insights.claim: 89% of surveyed companies reported AI-enabled attacks in the past 12 months, and 35% experienced significant financial or operational impact from them.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI-enabled attack exposure is already near-universal rather than emerging, which supports cyber insurance repricing and makes security a board-level rather than IT-level budget line.
insights.quote: AI-enabled threats were reported by 89% of companies in the last year.
insights.locator: AI-enabled threats were reported by 89% of companies

insights.claim: The average surveyed company suffered three significant breaches and 25 sensitive data incidents in the past 12 months.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Breach frequency at this level normalizes incident cost into operating expense assumptions and strengthens the case for incident response and data security demand.
insights.locator: AI-enabled threats were reported by 89% of companies

insights.claim: Growing model capability plus the increasing availability of powerful open-source models is expected to keep AI-enabled attack volume rising.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Open-weight diffusion means offensive capability cannot be gated by frontier labs, so defensive demand is structurally decoupled from any single vendor's safety policy.
insights.quote: With AI models growing in capability and increasing availability of powerful open-source models, we expect this trend to continue.
insights.locator: AI-enabled threats were reported by 89% of companies

themes.theme: Vendor competitive order in AI security

insights.claim: CISOs prefer frontier AI labs as suppliers of AI-embedded cyber solutions, followed closely by cyber platform incumbents such as CrowdStrike and Microsoft.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Frontier labs are emerging as direct competitors in a security budget historically owned by platform vendors, a share shift worth tracking in CrowdStrike and Microsoft security disclosures.
insights.quote: CISOs prefer frontier AI labs for AI-embedded cyber solutions, followed closely by cyber platform incumbents like CrowdStrike and Microsoft.
insights.locator: Frontier AI labs and cyber platform incumbents are winning

insights.claim: Hyperscalers and startups lag far behind in AI-embedded cyber solutions and typically win contracts only through ease of integration or in niche security domains.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Cuts against the assumption that hyperscalers bundle their way into AI security; startup underwriting should require a genuine niche or integration wedge, not general capability.
insights.quote: Hyperscalers and startups are lagging far behind, often winning contracts due to ease of integration or niche security domains.
insights.locator: Frontier AI labs and cyber platform incumbents are winning

insights.claim: Incumbent security vendors are asking customers to pay more for AI-enabled features while AI-native startups attack established categories and new vendors form around AI-specific risks that barely existed a few years ago.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sets up a pricing-versus-displacement test: incumbents monetizing AI as an uplift are vulnerable if AI-native entrants prove better outcomes at the same price.
insights.locator: This is the new reality for CISOs

insights.claim: Many cybersecurity vendors overpromise on offerings that do not truly leverage AI and do not deliver better outcomes, while customers will pay more for tools that are genuinely effective.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Implies a widening dispersion inside the cyber sector, favoring pair trades of proven-efficacy vendors against AI-branded names whose claims are not outcome-backed.
insights.locator: For cybersecurity vendors, differentiation is key

insights.claim: Most CISOs have already consolidated their vendors in 18 of the 24 security product categories tracked, and consolidation is still accelerating.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: With three-quarters of categories already consolidated, remaining growth for most vendors must come from displacement, raising the bar for new-logo assumptions in cyber models.
insights.quote: most CISOs have already consolidated their vendors in 18 of the 24 product categories we track
insights.locator: Platform consolidation remains a significant trend

insights.claim: More mature organizations consolidate security vendors to reduce complexity while less mature ones consolidate primarily to save cost, so the same trend has two different buying logics.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Determines which pitch wins where: platform breadth and integration for mature buyers, price and bundling for immature ones, which in turn sets achievable gross margin by segment.
insights.locator: Platform consolidation remains a significant trend

insights.claim: Standalone category leaders can still win contracts, but mid-tier vendors may not differentiate enough to justify a contract as buyers cut vendor counts.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A barbell structure in cyber equities and private assets: own platforms or clear category leaders, avoid or short the undifferentiated middle, which is also the natural M&A supply.
insights.quote: for vendors, the middle ground is a dangerous place to be
insights.locator: Platform consolidation remains a significant trend

themes.theme: Investor framing of the AI-cyber trade

insights.claim: AI is not replacing the cybersecurity market but accelerating it, fueling more demand for both security incumbents and startups.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Directly rebuts the AI-disruption discount applied to security software, arguing the sector is a beneficiary rather than a victim of AI capability gains.
insights.quote: AI is not replacing the cybersecurity market—it is accelerating it and fueling more demand for security incumbents and startups.
insights.locator: For investors, our data shows

insights.claim: Among the roughly 300 surveyed cybersecurity leaders, no one has truly solved the AI security problem and everyone feels vulnerable.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Universal unsolved-problem status means budget is defensive and non-discretionary, which supports demand durability even through an IT spending downturn.
insights.quote: Among our respondents, no one has truly solved the problem and everyone feels vulnerable.
insights.locator: Bottom-line Implications

insights.claim: Buyers face simultaneous pressure to stretch budgets, reduce vendor complexity, and separate real innovation from AI-branded noise, producing a more selective rather than uniformly expanding cybersecurity market.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sector-level growth will mask sharply divergent company outcomes, so index-style exposure to cyber underperforms selective exposure to proven category winners.
insights.quote: The result is a more selective cybersecurity market.
insights.locator: The result is a more selective cybersecurity market
